title: Ahrefs Shared Account: Safe Sharing & Team Access Guide
content:
Can you share an Ahrefs account with your team? The answer depends on how you provide access.

Ahrefs is a popular SEO research platform used for backlink analysis, keyword research, competitor analysis, rank tracking, and technical website auditing. For freelancers and agencies, having multiple people work with the same SEO data can make collaboration easier.

However, there is an important difference between adding authorized users to an Ahrefs workspace and sharing one login across multiple people.

Ahrefs supports team collaboration through eligible subscription plans, where invited members use their own accounts. Sharing a single person's login credentials is not an authorized substitute for additional user seats.

This guide explains how Ahrefs shared accounts work in 2026, how to invite team members, what permissions are available, the risks of unofficial group buy access, and how to choose an appropriate setup for your budget.

What Is an Ahrefs Shared Account?

An Ahrefs shared account generally refers to a subscription or workspace used by more than one person.

However, the phrase can describe two different arrangements:

  • Official Ahrefs workspace sharing: An account owner invites additional authorized users, who sign in with their own credentials and receive access according to their assigned roles.
  • Unofficial shared-login access: Multiple people use the same username and password, sometimes through a third-party group buy service.

These arrangements are not equivalent.

Official workspace access is designed for collaboration within Ahrefs' subscription and permission system. Unofficial credential sharing can violate Ahrefs' terms and lead to account restrictions.

For teams that need reliable access, the official workspace model is the recommended approach.

Understanding Ahrefs Account Sharing

The Official Way: Ahrefs Workspace Members

Ahrefs allows eligible subscribers to invite additional people to their workspace.

Each invited user signs in with a separate account, while the workspace provides access to supported SEO tools and shared resources.

Depending on the subscription, workspace administrators can manage members, assign roles, and control access to projects and folders.

This approach helps teams collaborate without distributing a single password.

Ahrefs currently supports adding workspace members on eligible Lite and higher plans. The Starter plan does not support additional users.

For current requirements, consult the official Ahrefs workspace member guide.

The Unofficial Way: Ahrefs Group Buy Accounts

Some third-party services advertise shared Ahrefs access at a lower cost than purchasing an official subscription.

These arrangements may involve multiple unrelated customers accessing the same subscription or using a managed interface.

However, paying a third-party operator does not automatically mean the access arrangement is authorized by Ahrefs.

Ahrefs states that individual login credentials must not be shared between users and that unauthorized sharing can result in restrictions or suspension.

Group buy services may also introduce privacy, security, and service availability concerns.

Before purchasing any third-party Ahrefs access, verify how the service operates and whether the arrangement complies with Ahrefs' current terms.

If you are exploring third-party options, review the current listing on our Ahrefs Group Buy product page and compare terms carefully.

Common Misconceptions About Ahrefs Account Sharing

Myth 1: Sharing One Ahrefs Login Is Allowed

Some users assume that sharing one username and password with a colleague is equivalent to adding an authorized team member.

It is not.

Ahrefs requires individual users to have their own login credentials. Sharing a single login can trigger additional verification and account restrictions.

For legitimate collaboration, invite users through the workspace member system instead.

Myth 2: Group Buy Services Automatically Provide Authorized Access

A third-party service may advertise low-cost Ahrefs access, but that does not establish a licensing relationship with Ahrefs.

Unauthorized account sharing or resale may conflict with the original software terms.

Users should also consider whether their projects, research history, and account information could be exposed in a shared environment.

Myth 3: Every Team Member Needs a Completely Separate Subscription

Ahrefs supports additional members within eligible workspaces, so organizations do not necessarily need to purchase an entirely separate workspace subscription for every employee.

However, each person who requires independent access needs an appropriate authorized user seat.

The number of available seats and their cost depend on the subscription plan.

Myth 4: All Workspace Data Is Private to Each Member

Ahrefs offers project and folder sharing controls, but that does not mean every activity is private.

According to Ahrefs' workspace documentation, members share certain workspace data, including search history and keyword lists.

Workspace owners and administrators may also have broader access to projects and settings.

Teams handling confidential client information should understand these visibility rules before adding users.

How to Share an Ahrefs Account With Your Team

The recommended method is to add authorized workspace members rather than share login credentials.

Step 1: Check Your Ahrefs Subscription

Sign in to your Ahrefs account and confirm whether your subscription supports additional users.

Ahrefs Starter does not support additional members. Eligible Lite and higher subscriptions offer member management, subject to plan-specific limits and charges.

Step 2: Open Workspace Settings

Navigate to your account or workspace settings and locate the Members section.

Eligible accounts may also provide an Invite Members option through the workspace switcher.

Step 3: Invite Team Members

Enter the email addresses of the people you want to invite.

Each member should use their own Ahrefs login rather than the account owner's credentials.

Step 4: Assign Appropriate Roles

Choose the appropriate access level for each user.

Ahrefs supports roles such as Owner, Admin, and Member. Enterprise plans may provide additional guest access capabilities.

Assign administrative privileges only to people who need to manage workspace settings, subscriptions, or other users.

Step 5: Configure Project Sharing

Use available project and folder sharing settings to control which resources are accessible to specific members.

Remember that administrators may have broader visibility, and some workspace information is shared across members.

Step 6: Review Usage and Billing

Additional users may affect subscription charges and shared usage allowances.

Review seat limits, credits, exports, and billing information before inviting more users.

Who Should Use an Ahrefs Shared Workspace?

Small SEO Teams and Agencies

Agencies often need several employees to access keyword research, backlink reports, website audits, and ranking information.

An authorized Ahrefs workspace can support collaboration while providing member management and project sharing controls.

Before adding client-related information, confirm which users can access projects and other workspace data.

Freelancers and SEO Consultants

Freelancers who work with assistants, contractors, or clients may benefit from adding authorized users when their subscription supports it.

For occasional collaboration, compare the cost of additional seats against the actual frequency of use.

Not every freelancer needs a multi-user setup. Solo users may find an individual subscription more practical.

In-House Marketing Teams

Marketing departments can use a shared workspace to coordinate SEO research and maintain access to common projects.

Roles and project permissions can help organize work, although teams should not assume complete privacy between workspace members.

Who Should Avoid Unofficial Account Sharing?

Businesses handling confidential information, agencies with strict client agreements, and teams that depend on uninterrupted software access should avoid unauthorized shared-login arrangements.

These arrangements can create licensing, security, and continuity risks that outweigh the apparent subscription savings.

Ahrefs Workspace Roles and Permissions

Understanding workspace roles is important when several people collaborate on SEO projects.

Owner

The Owner is the account's primary owner and has broad control over subscription and workspace management.

Admin

Administrators can manage workspace settings, members, and subscription-related functions according to Ahrefs' permission system.

Member

Members can access workspace resources according to their assigned permissions and sharing settings.

Guest

Guest access is available under applicable Enterprise arrangements and is intended for more limited access to explicitly shared resources.

Important: Project-level permissions do not guarantee that all workspace data is private. Review Ahrefs' current access control documentation before using a shared workspace for sensitive projects.

Ahrefs Shared Account Pricing and User Seats

Ahrefs subscription pricing depends on the selected plan, included users, additional seats, and applicable usage allowances.

The Starter plan is designed for individual use and does not support additional users.

Eligible higher-tier plans allow additional workspace members, subject to plan-specific limits and billing rules.

Rather than relying on outdated pricing tables, check the current official Ahrefs pricing page before making a purchase.

When calculating the cost of team access, consider:

  • Base subscription price
  • Number of authorized users required
  • Additional seat charges
  • Shared credits and usage allowances
  • Reporting and export requirements
  • Monthly versus annual billing

Security Best Practices for Ahrefs Team Sharing

Even with authorized workspace access, account security remains important.

  • Use separate logins: Never distribute the account owner's password to other team members.
  • Enable two-factor authentication: Use available security protections for individual accounts.
  • Review member permissions: Give users only the access required for their work.
  • Remove former employees: Revoke access when someone leaves your organization.
  • Check project visibility: Understand which projects and workspace information are shared.
  • Monitor usage: Review subscription limits and additional seat charges.
  • Protect client data: Avoid exposing confidential information to unnecessary workspace members.

Is Ahrefs Shared Access Worth It for Small Teams and Freelancers?

Official Ahrefs workspace sharing can be useful when several authorized users need access to common SEO research resources.

For small agencies, the ability to manage members and projects may justify the additional subscription cost.

For freelancers who work independently, a single-user subscription may be sufficient.

Unofficial shared-login services may advertise lower prices, but they introduce risks involving licensing, account restrictions, data privacy, and access continuity.

The right choice depends on your team size, budget, required features, and sensitivity of the information being handled.

Alternatives to Unofficial Ahrefs Shared Accounts

If official multi-user Ahrefs access exceeds your budget, consider alternatives that do not depend on unauthorized credential sharing.

  • Ahrefs Free Tools: Explore available free SEO resources and website owner features.
  • Ahrefs Starter: Consider the official entry-level plan for individual research needs.
  • Google Search Console: Monitor organic search performance for websites you manage.
  • Other SEO Platforms: Compare software based on the research features you actually need.
  • Official Team Plans: Evaluate authorized additional users when collaboration is essential.

SEOGBTools also publishes information about SEO software and available tool access options. You can explore our SEO tools catalog, but any third-party Ahrefs offer should be evaluated against Ahrefs' licensing and access requirements.

Frequently Asked Questions About Ahrefs Shared Accounts

Can I share my Ahrefs account with another person?

You can invite additional authorized members to eligible Ahrefs workspaces. However, each person must use their own login credentials. Sharing one person's login is not the same as authorized workspace access.

Does Ahrefs allow multiple users?

Yes. Eligible subscription plans support additional workspace users, subject to plan-specific limits and charges.

Can I add users on Ahrefs Starter?

No. According to Ahrefs' current documentation, the Starter plan does not support additional users.

How do I invite someone to my Ahrefs workspace?

Open the Members section in your account settings or use the workspace invitation option, then enter the person's email and assign an appropriate role.

Is sharing an Ahrefs password allowed?

Ahrefs requires separate credentials for individual users. Sharing one login can trigger verification procedures and account restrictions.

Are Ahrefs group buy accounts safe?

Unofficial shared-login arrangements can create account security, privacy, licensing, and availability risks. A low advertised price does not guarantee authorized access.

Can team members see each other's Ahrefs research?

Some workspace information, including search history and keyword lists, is shared. Project and folder permissions provide additional controls, but administrators may have broader visibility.

How much does an additional Ahrefs user cost?

Pricing depends on the subscription plan and current billing rules. Check Ahrefs' official pricing and account settings for accurate charges.

Can I remove a team member from Ahrefs?

Yes. Workspace administrators can manage and remove members. Billing changes associated with user seats may take effect according to the subscription's billing rules.

Is an official Ahrefs workspace better for agencies?

For agencies requiring authorized access, individual user accounts, and defined permissions, an official workspace is generally more appropriate than unofficial shared credentials.

Key Takeaways

  • Ahrefs supports authorized multi-user collaboration through eligible workspaces.
  • Each user should have their own login credentials.
  • The Starter plan does not support additional workspace users.
  • Workspace roles and project permissions help manage access, but some data is shared.
  • Unofficial credential sharing can result in restrictions and security concerns.
  • Subscription costs and seat allowances should be verified against current official pricing.

Final Verdict: What Is the Safest Way to Share Ahrefs?

The safest supported way to share Ahrefs access is through an eligible official workspace with authorized user seats and individual login credentials.

This approach provides clearer account management, permissions, and licensing rights than distributing a single password across multiple people.

For freelancers, the best option may be an individual plan. For agencies and growing teams, authorized workspace members can support collaboration while keeping access organized.

Before choosing any third-party shared-access service, review its licensing arrangements, privacy protections, support policies, and the original software provider's terms.
